title: appsettings.json layering and environment overrides
hook: appsettings.json holds your defaults; appsettings.Development.json and appsettings.Production.json layer on top based on ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT — the same pattern Express apps use with NODE_ENV-specific config files.

blocks.text: appsettings.json is the base configuration file loaded for every environment. The host then loads appsettings.{Environment}.json where {Environment} matches IHostEnvironment.EnvironmentName (Development, Staging, Production, or custom). Keys in the environment-specific file override the base file. ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT (or DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT) selects which overlay applies. This layering keeps shared defaults in one place and environment deltas in separate files.

entries.plainDefinition: Base settings file committed to source control. Contains structure and non-secret defaults.
entries.example: Logging levels, allowed hosts, feature section scaffolding.

entries.plainDefinition: Overrides loaded when EnvironmentName is Development. Often enables Swagger and verbose logging.
Environment variable that sets the active environment name and selects which appsettings overlay loads.
entries.example: launchSettings.json sets it to Development for F5 debugging.

entries.plainDefinition: Abstraction exposing EnvironmentName, ApplicationName, and ContentRootPath.

blocks.text: Without layering, teams duplicate entire config files per environment or hard-code if/else blocks in Program.cs. Staging should mirror Production structure but point at test databases. A classic production incident: appsettings.Production.json missing a key falls back to Development connection string from base appsettings.json. Environment variables from Kubernetes still override both files — the full picture is base JSON + environment JSON + env vars.

blocks.title: Never commit secrets to appsettings
blocks.body: Base and environment JSON files are in git. Put secrets in user secrets (local), environment variables (containers), or Azure Key Vault (production). appsettings should contain placeholders or Key Vault references, not live passwords.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Read ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT
items.body: Defaults to Production if unset. launchSettings.json sets Development during local debug.

items.title: Load appsettings.json
items.body: Required base file. Missing file throws at startup unless you customize the host.

items.title: Load appsettings.{Environment}.json
items.body: Optional overlay. Development and Production files are common; Staging for pre-prod.

items.title: Later providers override
items.body: User secrets, environment variables, and command line still override JSON values.

diagram.title: appsettings layering by environment
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  ENV[ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT] --> PICK{Environment name}
  PICK -->|Development| DEV[appsettings.Development.json]
  PICK -->|Production| PROD[appsettings.Production.json]
  PICK -->|Staging| STG[appsettings.Staging.json]
  BASE[appsettings.json] --> MERGE[Merged IConfiguration]
  DEV --> MERGE
  PROD --> MERGE
  STG --> MERGE
  MERGE --> ENVVARS[Env vars override JSON]

snippet.label: Base appsettings.json
snippet.explanation: Shared defaults across all environments. No secrets. Structure matches your options classes for clean binding.

snippet.label: appsettings.Development.json overrides
snippet.explanation: Only keys that differ from base need appear. OrdersApi:BaseUrl overrides; TimeoutSeconds inherits 30 from base.

snippet.label: Conditional behavior by environment in Program.cs
snippet.explanation: IHostEnvironment drives runtime behavior beyond JSON. IsDevelopment, IsProduction, and IsEnvironment check the name set by ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT.

snippet.label: launchSettings.json sets local environment
snippet.explanation: F5 debugging uses launchSettings profiles. This file is not deployed — only affects local Visual Studio / VS Code / dotnet run. Production sets ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT in the container manifest.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Shipping with ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development in Docker. Putting production connection strings in appsettings.json because 'the Production file will override' — env vars in K8s should be the source of truth for secrets. Creating appsettings.Staging.json but never setting Staging in the deployment — app runs as Production with wrong overlay. Using IsDevelopment() to gate security features that should always be on in Production.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: on startup log IHostEnvironment.EnvironmentName and a hash of non-secret config keys — mismatches between expected Staging and actual Production explain wrong Swagger exposure. Health check endpoint can expose environment name in a controlled way for ops dashboards. When debugging 'wrong database,' dump GetDebugView() locally and compare K8s deployment env block to appsettings layering. Custom environments (Integration, QA) require explicit ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT in CI pipelines and matching appsettings.{Name}.json files.

Harder to see full config without cluster access

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Not knowing default environment is Production when unset. Saying appsettings.Production.json is required — it is optional. Confusing ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT with DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT (both work; ASPNETCORE_ is conventional for web). Claiming environment JSON overrides environment variables.

interviewTakeaways: appsettings.json is the base; appsettings.{Environment}.json overlays based on ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT.
Environment variables and command line still override JSON — layering is not the final word.
Production tip: never set ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development in containers; log EnvironmentName at startup for audit.
60s: Base JSON loads first, environment file second, both optional except base. ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT selects overlay. Defaults to Production. Env vars override JSON with __ naming.
Follow-up: how do user secrets fit into the chain for local Development?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'Production file always loads' gets you rejected — only the file matching EnvironmentName loads, and it is optional.
Development environment in production Docker image — exposes Swagger and detailed errors.
Strong answer: 'Base + environment overlay, then env vars win. I keep secrets out of JSON, verify ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT in K8s manifests, and use IsProduction() for security middleware.'
introducedIn: ASP.NET Core 1.0 appsettings pattern; standard in all .NET versions

jsTsCorrelations.note: Express apps use NODE_ENV to pick config files manually. ASP.NET Core's host loads appsettings.{Environment}.json automatically — no require() switch statement.
NestJS often uses .env.development and ConfigModule envFilePath arrays. ASP.NET Core ties file name directly to IHostEnvironment.EnvironmentName.
